title: Regeneration not ex operibus per apostolic rule
source_text: XX. Proinde cum nostra regeneratio, seu sanctificatio in solidum gratiae divinae tribui debeat, certum est, juxta sensum & stylum Apostolicum, illam non esse ex operibus; ne-que nos ex operibus regenerari, seu sanctificari, id est, operum nostrorum merito & efficacia sanctos justosque coram Deo reddi. Nam Apostoli sententia sive regula gene-ralis haec est, Si per gratiam, non ex operibus, alioqui gratia jam non est gratia: si ex ope-ribus, jam non est gratia, alioquin opus jam non est opus. Rom. 11. 6.
pass_a_gloss: Accordingly, since our regeneration or sanctification ought to be ascribed wholly to divine grace, it is certain, according to the apostolic sense and style, that it is not of works; nor are we regenerated or sanctified of works—that is, made holy and just before God by the merit and efficacy of our works. For the Apostle's sentence or general rule is this: If by grace, then not of works, otherwise grace is no longer grace; if of works, then it is no longer grace, otherwise work is no longer work (Romans 11:6).
pass_b_english: Since regeneration is wholly of grace, it is not ex operibus by apostolic rule—Rom 11:6.
Grace and works as meritorious cause exclude each other.

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1054.
